conventions.convention: The mass matrix is constant SPD; c and V are smooth, 1 ≤ m < d, and regularity means rank Dc(q) = m. Consistency requires both c(q) = 0 and J(q)M⁻¹p = 0.
The canonical form is ω₀ = Σ dqᵢ ∧ dpᵢ = −d(pᵀdq); constrained cotangent coordinates use π = Dφᵀp.

RATTLE uses signed h, force-level multipliers with impulses hJᵀλ and hJᵀμ, position residual h⁻²c(q₁), and tangency residual h⁻¹J(q₁)M⁻¹p₁. Both selected multiplier limits equal half the continuous multiplier; the h = 0 map is the identity.

Finite-solver success means only that both residual tolerances were met. Inputs must be consistent, branch domains must admit all evaluations, and evaluation primitives and exact factorization/solve backends must terminate.

Repeated finite solves restore consistency using the local retractions before the next input. Their global error is measured against exact-solve RATTLE on fixed-time grids within nested compact phase tubes.

load_bearing.statement: On each compact regular phase subset, the scaled RATTLE equations have unique smooth local multiplier branches with common sufficiently small signed-step range, uniformly bounded derivatives of each fixed finite order, and uniformly invertible multiplier Jacobians. At h = 0 both Jacobians equal −A(q).

The regular configuration manifold has dimension d−m. In a configuration chart with T = Dφ and G = TᵀMT, a cotangent coordinate π has unique consistent ambient representative p = MTG⁻¹π; the restricted canonical form is Σ dxⱼ ∧ dπⱼ and is symplectic.

On local neighborhoods covering a compact consistent phase set there are smooth retractions Πⱼ onto the phase manifold, identity on consistent inputs, satisfying ‖Πⱼ(q,p)−(q,p)‖ ≤ Cⱼ(‖c(q)‖₂ + ‖J(q)M⁻¹p‖₂), with a common constant on a finite cover.
On the selected local branch, exact RATTLE sends consistent states to consistent states and satisfies Ψ₋ₕ ∘ Ψₕ = id and Ψₕ ∘ Ψ₋ₕ = id whenever both branch steps remain in the regular chart.

Successful branch-local finite solves satisfy position error ≤ Ch²εq and momentum error ≤ C|h|(εq+εp). Under the stated nested-tube and consistency-restoration hypotheses, sufficiently small fixed scaled residuals give O(ε) trajectory error relative to exact-solve RATTLE; O(h²) scaled residuals give O(h²) trajectory error and raw constraint residuals O(h⁴), O(h³).
For r ∈ {1,2}, a C^(k+r) residual whose h-derivatives through order r−1 vanish at h = 0 has a C^k extension after division by h^r, with the stated factorial formula for its mixed derivatives at zero.

Under the stated compact regular convex-coordinate tube hypothesis, selected exact RATTLE branches with O(h²) consistent initial error remain in the regular chart for sufficiently large N and have maximum fixed-time grid error ≤ C_T h².

seams_checked.note: The residual-units definition and finite Newton/chord procedure are used within their actual domains and backend contracts. RATTLE supplies its own scaled inverse estimates; neither solver success nor residual magnitude is treated as an independent forward-error certificate. No reverse RATTLE premise is imported by the inspected supplier text.

The inspected DAE interface requires an invertible algebraic Jacobian and expressly excludes higher-index systems. RATTLE does not apply that index-one reduction to unreduced holonomic constraints: its flow, multiplier branches, and restoration estimates are proved locally. The prerequisite is contextual, and the inspected DAE statements do not depend on RATTLE.

The inspected geometric suppliers establish the canonical Jacobian identity for admitted unconstrained shears and their compositions. RATTLE does not infer constrained symplecticity from those results; it proves the restricted cotangent pullback identity using its discrete Lagrangian. The inspected supplier arguments use no RATTLE premise.
